recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow **Liquid Domain** with **FLIP** enabled and **mesh generation** enabled, driven by an **inflow** (use_plane_init=True) positioned above the glass. For stable volume and controllable splash/turbulence, tune the liquid particle system controls documented under Liquid domain settings: **Particle Radius** (primary control for apparent volume loss/gain/leaks), **Sampling** (more particles sampled per step), and **Randomness** (0.0 for more laminar inflow; higher for more turbulent inflow). For renderable wine surface quality, apply domain mesh-quality parameters (concavity + smoothing passes) and ensure the glass is a clean collision object (optionally add an invisible collision “disc” at the bowl–stem junction to prevent leakage through thin geometry).

domain.particle_radius_guidance: If liquid seems to disappear (volume loss/leaks), increase Particle Radius; if too much liquid is produced, decrease it.
domain.sampling_guidance: Higher Sampling will sample more particles; note resampling occurs every simulation step.
domain.randomness_guidance: 0.0 yields uniform (less random) particle placement for a more laminar inflow; higher values increase turbulence in inflow regions.

warnings: Liquid domain docs note **Particle Radius** is the first parameter to adjust when the sim appears to **leak / lose volume** (increase it) or **gain volume** (decrease it).
Liquid domain docs note **particle resampling occurs every simulation step**; increasing Sampling/particle counts can increase cost significantly.
Liquid domain docs note **Randomness=0.0** gives uniform particle placement (more laminar inflow); higher randomness increases turbulence in inflow regions, which can change splash character.
Pattern guidance: thin glass/stem geometry can allow liquid to appear to escape; adding a hidden collision “disc” effector at the bowl–stem junction can prevent leakage artifacts.
